After I finish my lunch, I will open the messaging app, type “Hi, enjoyed our chat,” and hit send – under 30 seconds. If the day feels rough, just open the app and tap send without typing anything else.

It works because a concrete, low‑effort outreach lowers the barrier to building a connection.

b.advice: Link the greeting to the moment you unlock your computer (implementation intention). After you log in, walk straight to the nearest inspection station (habit stack) and say the exact phrase “Buenos días, ¿cómo va la línea hoy?” If you’re pressed for time, fall back to the 5‑second version “Buenos días”. Immediately after the response, note the inspector’s answer on a sticky note (self‑monitoring) and mark a check‑off on a simple tally sheet. This concrete cue‑action‑record loop makes the habit easy to start, hard to forget, and provides visible proof of completion.

t.lesson: After you log in, walk to the nearest inspection station and ask the inspector, “¿Qué observó ayer que podríamos mejorar?” Write the answer on a sticky note. This tiny habit shows you value their view and builds humility.
